AMSTERDAM WEEKEND TIPS: 10, 11, 12 & 13 SEPTEMBER

➊ Open this week: major Yayoi Kusama exhibition at the Stedelijk

You'll want to put this one on your list for the weekend (or one of the upcoming weekends): on Friday, September 11, a major retrospective of Yayoi Kusama opens at the Stedelijk Museum . The exhibition takes you through more than seventy years of her work, from paintings and sculptures to fashion, performances, and, of course, her famous installations full of dots and mirrors. I already have tickets for Saturday myself!

One of the highlights is a new version of one of Kusama's iconic installations, in which patterns and reflections create a sense of infinity. Additionally, historical works that have not previously been shown in Europe are on display. Following her recent passing, the exhibition is moreover a posthumous tribute to her life and work.

Book tickets

From: Friday, September 11, 2026 to January 17, 2027
Location: Stedelijk Museum Amsterdam, Museumplein
Tickets: book your tickets in advance here >>

Tip: combine Kusama with a special dinner at Sandberg

Would you like to turn your visit to the new Yayoi Kusama exhibition into a complete evening? Café Restaurant Sandberg, located in the Stedelijk, is organizing a special series of dinners inspired by Kusama's work together with chef Schilo van Coevorden.

Schilo, known among other things as the founder of Taiko, translates the colors, shapes, and repetition from Kusama's work into a five-course menu. There are only seven evenings on which you can book this special dinner, so this is one to reserve in advance. More info & reservations >>

Menu: 5 courses for €69 per person
Location: Café Restaurant Sandberg, Stedelijk Museum, Museumplein 10
When: September 11, 12, 18, 19, 24, 25 and 26

Book online

➋ Our favorite weekend markets in Amsterdam listed for you:

You say weekend, you say browsing markets. These are the weekend markets in Amsterdam to visit.

First Sunday Market at Amstel 1

Great news for everyone who loves browsing the Sunday Market: the very first edition will take place on Sunday, September 13 at Amstel 1 in the Stopera. More than fifty designers, artists, and artisans will present their work in De Lichtstraat and outside. Think ceramics, jewelry, art, design, and other unique finds.

You're also in the right place for delicious food. In collaboration with The Food Line-up, there are more than ten food stands. An extra treat: the market coincides with the festive opening of the renovated indoor street of the Stopera.

Date: Sunday September 13
Time: 11.00 AM - 17.00 PM
Location: Amstel 1, Stopera, Amsterdam-Centrum
Free access

Vintage market during Summer @ H'ART

Saturday is the final edition of Summer @ H'ART at the H'ART Museum. In the courtyard, you can browse past the vintage finds from Block Market from 11:00 AM to 4:30 PM, and there will be delicious food, drinks, and live music.

There is also an upcycling workshop by Atelier Amsterdam Offline. Bring a piece of clothing of your own for this, or use an item you just scored at the vintage market. You must reserve a spot for the workshop in advance. The afternoon will conclude with a live performance by Stokers.

Date: Saturday, September 12
Time: 11.00 AM - 16.30 PM
Location: H'ART Museum, Amstel 51, Amsterdam

Pure Market

The ultimate Sunday market for a delightful afternoon with food trucks and local products. Featuring over 70 artisanal entrepreneurs, lots of delicious food and drinks, and a fun atmosphere for the kids. Whether you're having drinks with friends or want to pick up tasty treats to take home… The Pure Markt is open until 18 pm. My tip: grab a delicious grilled chicken to pop straight into the oven on Sunday evening!
Dates & locations: September 13 Amstelpark, September 20 – Amsterdamse Bos, September 27 – Park Frankendael

Harvest Festivals & Pick-Your-Own at the Olmenhorst

One of our favorite outings to celebrate the start of autumn: starting this weekend, you can once again pick apples and pears at Landgoed de Olmenhorst. This year, the start of the picking season is being given extra special attention with the Harvest Festivals, in collaboration with the Rollende Keukens and Cantina Mobilé.

In addition to picking your own fruit in the organic orchards, there is live music every weekend, delicious food and drinks, a market with artisanal products, and plenty of entertainment for the kids. Think a Ferris wheel, ponies, bungee jumping, and face painting. In short: the kind of autumn outing you can easily spend a whole day on. TIP: In this article, I share more tips for apple picking in the Amsterdam area >>

Date: every Saturday and Sunday up to and including October 25
Harvest Festival times: 10:00 – 21:00
Self-picking: Wednesday 1:00 PM – 5:00 PM and Saturday & Sunday 10:00 AM – 5:00 PM
Location: Landgoed de Olmenhorst, Lisserbroek
Admission: free, parking €6. More info >>

Sunday Market

Our favorite for a Sunday afternoon: shop at local makers, enjoy delicious food and live music, while the kids have fun. You can find the Sunday Market at various locations in Amsterdam.
Dates & locations: September 6 – Westergas

Amstel 1 Market

Every Friday and Saturday, you can shop for fresh products here directly from local farmers, producers, and chefs. Think artisanal bread, vegetables, delicacies, and other local flavors and ingredients.
Dates: Weekly on Friday and Saturday
Location: Amstel 1, Amsterdam

noordermarkt

Every Saturday, this is the place for your organic groceries, and on Mondays, you can shop for vintage, curiosities, and antiques.
Location: Noordermarkt 1, Amsterdam
Dates: Every Monday and Saturday morning

| TIP: don't miss the Lindengracht Market in the Jordaan on Saturday either >>

Javaplein Vintage Market

A small vintage market on Javaplein in East Amsterdam, where you can score that one special gem, from vintage clothing to accessories and lovely home decor items. Tip: go for a nice lunch afterwards at Bathhouse of Le French Café in the Javastraat.
Date: October 3
Location: Javaplein Oost, Amsterdam

| TIP: these are the tastiest stalls at almost every market: Dappermarkt , Ten Katemarkt & Albert Cuypmarkt.

The firm

Save the date for October! One of the nicest design markets in Amsterdam, where you browse among vintage furniture, art, fashion, vinyl, and design classics. With specialty coffee, good wine, and live music.
Dates: 3 & 4 October 2026
Location: Central Market, Amsterdam

❸ These are the events not to be missed in Amsterdam:

40th edition Open Monument Day Amsterdam

This weekend is Open Monument Day Amsterdam, and this 40th edition is one not to be missed. On Saturday 12 and Sunday 13 September, special monuments throughout the city will open their doors for free. A great opportunity to finally take a look inside places you wouldn't normally have access to.

The program includes the Amstel Hotel, the Van Gendthallen, historic canal houses, and Amsterdam's first skyscraper, among others. In addition to guided tours, there are activities throughout the city featuring dance, spoken word, film, and music. So check the program in advance and plan a route past the monuments you don't want to miss.

Date: Saturday 12 & Sunday 13 September
Location: various locations throughout Amsterdam
Admission: many participating monuments and activities are free
<strong> More info: </strong> view all locations & activities >>

Read My World Book Market in the Tolhuistuin

On Saturday, the Tolhuistuin will be dedicated to books, stories, and exceptional creators during the Read My World Book Market. Browse books by international festival guests and other writers, and combine the market with the free program organized throughout the day.

For example, you can participate in a collage workshop or a masterclass in literary translation, there is a book presentation with Massih Hutak, and the day concludes with a discussion about the Moluccan novel *Onder de sneeuw een Indisch graf* by Frans Lopulalan. You must register in advance for the workshop and masterclass.

Date: Saturday, September 12
Location: Tolhuistuin, Amsterdam-Noord
Free access. More info >>

Hanneke's Late Summer Party

Want to celebrate summer one last time? On Friday, September 11, Hannekes Boom is organizing the Late Summer Party. It starts after work with drinks on the terrace and hopefully one of those beautiful sunsets this waterside spot is known for. Later in the evening, the music gets louder and the dancing continues inside until deep into the night. Also nice: admission is free!

Date: Friday, September 11
Location: Hannekes Boom, Dijksgracht 4, Amsterdam
Free access

End of Summer Blockparty at Yellow House

Dance outside one last time before we truly wrap up the summer. On Sunday, September 13, YUSU is organizing an End of Summer Blockparty at Yellow House in Amsterdam-West. From 3:00 PM to 10:00 PM, there will be a massive line-up featuring WaxFiend, Zoë Janice, BVNDO, Malindi, Nathifa Efia, and YUSU Selectors, among others. Admission is completely free, but you do need to claim your spot in advance via the RSVP. Perfect for a Sunday afternoon with music that naturally transitions into early evening dancing.

Date: Sunday September 13
Time: 15.00 AM - 22.00 PM
Location: Yellow House, Danzigerbocht 45R, Amsterdam
Admission: free, RSVP in advance

Are you curious to know which new restaurants have opened? I have listed a few below. You can view the full list of new restaurants in Amsterdam here >>

Do you like to stay up to date on which restaurants are coming soon or opening shortly? We are starting to update the 'Coming Soon' list again. That way, you'll have something to chat about on your next dinner date!

Afternoon Tea at Mandarin Oriental Conservatory

In the mood to catch up properly over Afternoon Tea? At Mandarin Oriental Conservatorium, Amsterdam, you can join us for Notes of Summer from Thursday through Sunday. It is served in the hotel lobby, also known as The Living Room of Amsterdam, where it gets pleasantly busy later in the afternoon with hotel guests and Amsterdammers coming for drinks.

The Afternoon Tea consists of four savory dishes, six sweet creations, and freshly baked scones, all made in-house daily. The menu features seasonal fruit, botanical flavors, and refined pastries. You can choose the classic Afternoon Tea or the variant with champagne. I had the afternoon tea with my family recently and it is really delicious. We will definitely be back as soon as the autumn edition starts! More info & reservations >>

When: Thursday to Sunday
Time: reservations between 14:00 and 16:00
Location: Mandarin Oriental Conservatory, Amsterdam. 

© MO Amsterdam Afternoon Tea

Mexican Independence Day in Oaxaca

A good reason to dine at Oaxaca again this month: around Mexican Independence Day, Chiles en Nogada is on the menu. The green, white, and red colors refer to the Mexican flag, and you won't find this classic Mexican seasonal dish anywhere else in the Netherlands. It is made with roasted poblano peppers from their own garden, filled with a picadillo of meat, fruit, and almonds. Topped with a creamy walnut sauce with pomegranate and coriander. I have already tasted it, and it is so unique and delicious! I had never eaten it before.

The dish is traditionally made only when the main ingredients are in season and is available at Oaxaca as long as the poblanos from their own garden are available. Order the Margarita del Grito to go with it for the occasion. More info & reservations >>

When: through the end of October, while stocks last
Chiles and Nogada: € 32
Margarita del Grito: € 16
Location: Oaxaca, Spuistraat 239, Amsterdam

© Oxaca

Café Binnenvisser x Hector's London

You'll want to add this tip straight to your schedule for this Sunday. London wine bar Hector's is taking over Café Binnenvisser for a British Sunday lunch that transitions into dinner. Chef Cavan Power O'Keeffe is in the kitchen, and special bottles are being brought out of the cellar for the occasion. The takeover starts as early as 1:00 PM, so book in advance if you want to join us on Sunday. More info & reservations >>

Date: Sunday September 13
Time: from 15:30
Location: Café Binnenvisser, Bilderdijkstraat 36, Amsterdam

Restaurant Flore celebrates 5 years with special collaborations

Restaurant Flore is celebrating its fifth anniversary this month with a series of special events. The kick-off is this weekend with a collaboration with Bakkerij WOLF. From September 11 to 13, you can sample a special brioche × Japanese milk bread with cocoa-free chocolate spread at WOLF, made from leftover sourdough. Only fifty are produced per bakery per day. At WOLF in the Zuidas area, you can even score a katsu sando. Later this month, a dinner among the meadows at Lindenhoff will follow, as well as a special Flore reunion where former chefs, sommeliers, and managers will come together. More info >>

Flore x Bakkerij WOLF: 11, 12 & 13 September
Flore x Lindenhoff: September 18 & 19
Flore's reunion: September 20

Just opened: KISEKI Sake Bar & Food

New in the Helmersbuurt: KISEKI Sake Bar & Food, a cozy Japanese sake bar where you can also enjoy a great meal. The menu features Japanese dishes the chef enjoys himself, including kushiage: crispy fried skewers that KISEKI is introducing in Amsterdam. Order the selection of five to try different varieties. The menu also includes dishes such as crispy eggplant with miso, karaage, slow-cooked pork belly, and small rice bowls with marinated tuna, for example. Naturally, sake is the perfect accompaniment. The menu ranges from fresh and fruity to more complex varieties, and there is also shochu. It is a great place to discover this weekend for drinks with Japanese bites or a full meal. More info >>

Just opened: Bar François

A new wine bar opened on Douwes Dekkerstraat this week. Bar François is the place to be for natural wine and small plates, and it has a very cozy atmosphere. They are open from Wednesday to Thursday from 4:00 PM, so it is also perfect for having drinks in the late afternoon. More info >>

Just opened: Vermut in Oud-West

The Jan Pieter Heijestraat has gained another great spot. At Vermut, you can enjoy sitting on the terrace or inside the warm interior. Naturally, start your evening with a vermouth and be sure to ask them for advice if you are new to the vermouth game.

Afterward, be sure to order as much as possible from the menu to share. We have tasted almost everything by now and really liked everything. There are also surprising dishes on the menu that you won't find on every menu in Amsterdam yet. Definitely one to check out this weekend.

New in Oud-Zuid: gastropub 't Lemmeke brings London vibes to Amsterdam

Amsterdam has a new favorite. Behind 't Lemmeke is the same team as behind Wijmpje Beukers, Schotsheuvel, and De Zingende Zwaan, but this time it is all about the atmosphere of a classic British gastropub. Think candlelight, dark wooden accents, a cozy fireplace, and a friendly pub in the basement. 

We tasted almost the entire menu and can tell you already: this is a place you'll want to visit again. Go for a snacky dinner with the surprisingly good snack menu, or share a table full of dishes with friends. Sharing is allowed, but certainly not required. And when the weather is nice, the terrace is a lovely spot to start or end the evening.

Where: Van Breestraat 107A, Amsterdam-Zuid. More info & reservations >>

't Lemmeke © Your Little Black Book

➎ Fun weekend tips with the kids in Amsterdam

The weekend with kids is often already mega busy and packed with sports clubs, children's parties, and other obligations, but we still try to do one fun thing as a family every weekend. Now that the first days of autumn are approaching, we alternate being outdoors with fun indoor tips. This is what's on our list this weekend:

  • Sam & Julia at the Meervaart: fun for kids aged 3 to 7 who are fans of The Mouse House. On Saturday, the world of Sam & Julia comes to life in the theater during a 45-minute performance. There are two shows, at 1:00 PM and 3:00 PM. Saturday, September 12 | Meervaart, Meer en Vaart 300. More info & tickets >>
  • A fun tip for kids who would love to game all day: the Game On exhibition is temporarily on display at NEMO Science Museum. It’s not just about looking, because you can of course play yourself too. From a Nintendo from 1992 to the PlayStation 5, while you discover the role video games now play in our daily lives. Friday 11 to Sunday 13 September | NEMO Science Museum, Oosterdok 2. The exhibition runs until 25 October. More info >>
  • Visiting the Museum of Illusions with younger kids? Then September is a good month to go, as children aged 7 and up can enter for free until September 30. Inside, there are more than 70 optical illusions and interactive rooms to try out together. Friday, September 11 to Sunday, September 13, 10:00 AM–6:00 PM | Keizersgracht 676. More info >>
  • A whole weekend full of activities at Jeugdland: on Saturday from 10:30 to 11:30, there is a toddler and preschooler club for kids aged 2 to 5, featuring storytelling and nature adventures. From 11:00, children aged 6 and up can join the garden club. Sunday starts at 11:00 with the barefoot and sensory path, featuring a mud bath, tasting station, and sensory bin, among other things. Afterwards, from 13:00 to 16:00, there is Maakland, where kids aged 6 and up can hammer, build, and do odd jobs. Many activities are free and require no registration. Jeugdland Amsterdam, Valentijnkade 131. View the full program >>
  • Another fun Sunday tip for younger kids: Poppentheater Koos Kneus is playing De streken van meneer Piep! for children aged 2 to 6. Includes face painting and is exactly the kind of old-fashioned, cozy theater outing for a rainy morning. More info >>
  • Feeling like getting outside? A new art route has been open in the Amsterdamse Bos since this weekend. Along the walk, there are seven artworks that encourage you to look at nature in a different way. It's fun to combine with a long walk in the woods and a treat along the way. More info >>
  • It is also the season to go apple picking again. Around Amsterdam, there are various orchards where you can head out into the fields yourself. We have just completely re-selected and updated our favorite addresses. See where you can pick apples here >>
  • A rainy day? As far as I'm concerned, NEMO Science Museum remains one of the best indoor outings with kids. Almost everything here revolves around trying, experimenting, and discovering for yourself, so you can easily spend a few hours there. View tickets for NEMO >>
  • Do you have the updated ARTIS Aquarium Have you seen it yet? After the major restoration, the aquarium is finally open again this summer. You will not only see special fish and other aquatic animals there, but also discover how important water is for all living things. Read more about the new ARTIS Aquarium here >>
  • Haven't been to Barbie: The Dream Experience in Noord yet? You walk through various colorful Barbie worlds, and there is plenty to see and do for kids along the way. This month, there are also family tickets and a 4-for-3 ticket deal. View tickets >>
  • Are you looking for a fun and educational activity for kids? At Bricks & Robots, children build their own robots with LEGO® and learn to program through play. My son took a course here himself and really enjoyed it. Read more about Bricks & Robots here >>
  • More fun museums with kids? From the Maritime Museum en Allard Pierson to Wereldmuseum, Micropia en STREETWe have put together the best addresses in Amsterdam. View the best museums for children here >>
  • Do the kids mainly need to run, climb, and clamber around to their heart's content? Save our list of indoor playgrounds for a rainy weekend. View the indoor playgrounds here >>
  • With slightly older kids, we also always enjoy an arcade. Think air hockey, Mario Kart, VR games, bowling, or glow-in-the-dark minigolf. Check out the best arcades here >>
  • The Kinderkookkafé remains one of those classics that every generation enjoys. Kids get to work in the kitchen themselves, set the table, and then, of course, eat what they have made. More info >>
  • In the mood to grab a bite to eat somewhere afterwards? Our guide to kid-friendly restaurants in Amsterdam has been completely updated, from pizza and burgers to places where children have a bit more space. View the kid-friendly restaurants here >>
  • Want to get out of town for a bit? Pumpkin season has begun! Throughout the Netherlands, you can find pumpkin farms where you can pick out pumpkins and sometimes even pick them yourself. Great for a sunny autumn day and a perfect excuse for a short road trip. View 19 pumpkin farms in the Netherlands here >>
  • Here is another fun tip for a trip just outside the city: put on your hiking boots and go look for gnomes with the kids. Scattered throughout the Netherlands are gnome trails through the forest, complete with gnome hats and tasks to complete along the way. Especially fun with younger children. View the best gnome trails in the Netherlands here >>
